column3: The Hebrew actively says Gilead fathered Jephthah; BSB gives the relationship as “Gilead was his father”.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the sons of the wife” as they grow up; BSB uses a relative clause without that repetition.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Jephthah’s name when the men gather to him.
The Hebrew calls the Ammonites “the sons of Ammon”.
The Hebrew repeats both “the sons of Ammon” and “Israel”; BSB uses pronouns to continue the war clause.
The Hebrew explicitly names Jephthah as the person addressed.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats the elders of Gilead and describes becoming their head; BSB uses “they” and “leader”.
The Hebrew explicitly names the elders of Gilead and says the LORD gives them “before me”; BSB uses “them” and “to me”.
The Hebrew calls the LORD the one hearing between them; BSB calls Him their witness.
The Hebrew says Jephthah spoke all his words; BSB says he repeated all his terms.
The Hebrew asks “What is between me and you?” and explicitly says the king came “to me”; BSB asks what he has against Jephthah.
The Hebrew uses singular Israel for coming up and taking the land, then a plural pronoun for what must be restored; BSB has plural “they” and singular “it”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has a singular “he said to him” and joins the two lands with “and” under the negation; BSB uses an infinitive and “or”.
The Hebrew uses the image “Sea of Reeds”; BSB gives the conventional name “Red Sea”.
The Hebrew request is “let me pass”, singular; BSB has “let us pass”, plural.
The Hebrew repeats Moab’s name three times and uses the image of the rising sun for the eastern side; BSB condenses the repetitions.
The Hebrew names Sihon twice as king and repeats Israel as speaker. The request begins “let us pass” but ends “my place”; BSB has “our own place”.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Sihon and uses a plural verb for encamping; BSB keeps the actions under a singular subject.
The Hebrew uses the collective singular “the Amorite”; BSB has plural “the Amorites”.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “all the territory of the Amorite”; BSB says “all the land”.
The Hebrew uses the collective singular “the Amorite”; BSB has plural “the Amorites”.
The Hebrew’s second clause speaks of what the LORD dispossessed before them; BSB instead describes what He granted them.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew twice calls dependent towns “daughters” and explicitly names the sides of the Arnon; BSB has “villages” and “banks”.
The Hebrew describes the other party as doing evil in the present and explicitly names both peoples as sons; BSB uses “have done me wrong” and plural people names.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the Spirit was upon Jephthah and explicitly repeats Mizpah of Gilead; BSB says the Spirit came and replaces the second place name with “there”.
The Hebrew repeats the root for vowing and separately says “he said”; BSB introduces the vow with a single verb.
